note: How the show is put together. Everything a listener can change is in profile.json; this is the show's own craft. Draft 1 (14 Oct 2026), for Parth's review.

segments.name: Cold open
segments.about: One or two lines on the biggest moment for the listener, said in its mood. No greeting before it.

segments.name: Your teams
segments.about: Each die-hard item, highest stake first: the result, how it happened, what it means (table, series, standings), what is next.

segments.name: Rival Watch
segments.about: Only on a day a rival lost, drew or went out. Short and gleeful. Left out entirely on any other day, with no line about it.

segments.name: Also on your list
segments.about: Follow and big-moment items, brisk: a result and one line of why it matters.

segments.name: Around the grounds
segments.about: The Wider Pitch and The Sidelines: football and other sport that several outlets are leading with. Quick hits.

segments.name: Coming up
segments.about: The listener's fixtures in the next seven days, in their time zone, with what is at stake.

moods.elated: elated, loud, laughing with relief and joy
moods.relieved: relieved, a big exhale, then smiling
moods.gutted: gutted, slower and quieter, no laughter
moods.angry: angry and blunt, short sentences, no laughter
moods.heartbroken: heartbroken, slow and quiet, no laughter
moods.gleeful: gleeful, enjoying it, a grin in the voice

mood_rules.note: Read top to bottom; the first rule that matches sets the mood. Facts the rules use are worked out by code from the data (engine/fetch/*.mjs): won, lost, drew, big, close, came_from_behind, lead_lost, late_decider, conceded_late, red_card, upset, eliminated, title, podium, dnf, finished_low, preseason, stage, derby (against a rival), losing_run (lost the two before), winless_run (no win in the three before), winning_run (won the three before).

intensity.note: How strongly the mood is played, 1 to 5: the listener's care (die-hard 3, follow 2, big moments 1), one more for a final, a knockout, a derby, a title or going out, one more for a dramatic match (big margin, comeback, lead thrown away, late decider, upset, a run ended or extended). Pre-season and friendlies stay at 1. The Fan plays it at this strength, the Anchor one lower.

big_clubs.note: Clubs whose upsets and heavy defeats are news to any football fan (Around the grounds). ESPN's names.

cricket_tiers.note: Men's international sides by strength, for upsets and big wins (Around the grounds).

around.note: At most two results or stories from outside the listener's list, only when they clear min_drama (engine/fetch/elsewhere.mjs); none on a quiet day. Draft for discussion with Parth (15 Oct).

hosts.voice_style: A young man in his twenties, a sports fan, warm and casual; animated when he is happy, quiet when he is disappointed, always natural, never shouting.
hosts.about: the Fan. Warm, casual, emotionally invested: Madrid wins, Barcelona misery and Verstappen magic all hit him personally. He carries the listener's loyalties and feels every result out loud, at the strength the pack gives, in his own reactions; he makes bold calls about what will happen next.

hosts.voice_style: An older man, a calm and experienced sports broadcaster with a mature, gravelly voice.
hosts.about: the Anchor. Older in temperament, gravelly, precise and composed. Keeps the facts straight, explains the table and the series, asks the question a listener would, and quietly exposes Kylo's nonsense. Leads Around the grounds and Coming up.

title: Side Effects of Sports
signoff: That's Side Effects of Sports for today. Same time tomorrow.

sport_words.note: How code tells a story's sport from its headline, for skip_sports. Plain words, editable.

description: A daily sports show made for one fan: what happened to his teams and players, felt the way he feels it, and what is coming next.
dynamic: Kylo feels the result. Dhruv remembers what Kylo said before it happened.
